source.title: NysAct: A Scalable Preconditioned Gradient Descent using Nyström Approximation
source.authors: Hyunseok Seung; Jaewoo Lee; Hyunsuk Ko

record.file_problem: Full paper text is supplied; no truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizers and batch sizes on natural image-classification tasks, reporting test accuracy and training behavior; it tests parts of V4 and V5 conceptually but does not test memorization, generalization measures, or the other versions.
record.gate_note: Tables 2 and 4 report test accuracy for optimizer comparisons; the paper also explicitly describes training-loss and test-accuracy behavior in Results text. Figure 5's batch-size comparison is figure-only; only the textual summary is recorded. Resource and convergence results do not measure the claim's training/test generalization gap and are omitted.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares adaptive optimizers with momentum SGD using held-out image-classification accuracy (V4), and varies batch size at a fixed 100-epoch budget (V5). These comparisons bear on the claims despite being embedded in an optimizer-development paper. It is not an original source for either version.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that NysAct reduces preconditioning costs while retaining fast convergence and strong test accuracy. Their broad accuracy claim needs the reported exceptions: FOOF generally leads on CIFAR, and NysAct trails SGD and AdamW on ImageNet ResNet-50 and AdamW on DeiT-S. The record correctly describes Adam/AdamW's CIFAR disadvantage and AdamW's strong DeiT-S performance.
record.recipe_differences: The paper compares optimizer methods on natural image classification and reports test accuracy; it does not use the original claim's random-label or generalization-gap measurements. It uses fixed epoch budgets and optimizer-specific settings, with CIFAR hyperparameter grid search for FOOF and NysAct.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and architecture change the optimizer ranking: AdamW trails SGD on reported CIFAR cases and ResNet-50, but beats SGD on DeiT-S; batch size is described as reducing NysAct test accuracy moderately.
record.peer_reviewed: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (BigData) [Services Society]; extended version identifies the published version as IEEE BigData 2024.
record.problems: The study does not measure training error versus test error or random-label memorization. Several optimizer outcomes are reported only as accuracies, without a training-error comparison; ImageNet accuracy tables provide no uncertainty. Batch-size results are figure-only and the text supplies no exact values.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. The CIFAR Adam/AdamW and SGD test accuracies and the ImageNet SGD/AdamW results are recorded separately by model, dataset, epoch budget, and method. Figure 5 batch-size plot is retained as a figure-only row because the prose explicitly describes its direction.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.

A controlled tuning-budget comparison, broader tuning as a remedy, switching from Adam to SGD, and language benchmarks. AdamW is evaluated, but its isolated recovery effect is not established because its weight decay differs from Adam's. Early convergence statements do not establish equal or better final training performance.
Longer training or recipe adaptation as remedies for the batch-size penalty, workload-dependent thresholds, and language models.
Controlled dropout addition or removal, including interactions with dataset size and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Removal of memorized examples versus random removal and retraining.

missing.what: Extract the omitted CIFAR-100 optimizer comparisons from Table 2. At 100/200 epochs, SGD, Adam and AdamW accuracies respectively are: ResNet-32, 70.47/70.67, 67.16/67.90, 65.23/67.04%; ResNet-110, 71.44/72.48, 70.10/71.22, 68.88/70.59%; DenseNet-121, 79.63/80.32, 73.48/73.49, 75.51/76.30%. Preserve the table's uncertainties.

Figure 5 also compares KFAC, Eva and FOOF across batch sizes 128, 256, 512 and 1024 at 100 epochs. Appendix C describes batch-related degradation and greater stability for NysAct. Add separate baseline-method rows if the plotted directions can be established; the supplied text does not resolve their individual magnitudes.
missing.locator: Figure 5, final subplot; Appendix C, Essential Hyperparameters

record.verdict_notes: Table 7 gives fixed optimizer-specific settings, including different weight decay for AdamW; it does not document comparable learning-rate searches for SGD, Adam and AdamW. V4 verdicts therefore apply to the reported recipes. Held-out accuracy comparisons suffice to test V4's main performance claim without a numerical training–test gap. Missing numeric plot values do not negate the explicit directional V5 result.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Broader tuning, switching from Adam to SGD, decoupled weight decay as a recovery, and word-level language models.
Large-batch effects are described for NysAct and baselines, but Figure 5 provides no recoverable numeric results.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring retrained test accuracy.
